html:
The Duar War was fought between Bhutan and British India in 1864 and 1865 over the Duars, the fertile plains along the foot of the hills.

Bhutan had long held the Duars and raided across them. After a British envoy was humiliated at the Bhutanese court in 1864, Britain sent troops. Bhutanese forces won a surprise victory at Dewangiri, but the British returned in strength.

Under the Treaty of Sinchula in 1865 Bhutan gave up the Duars for a yearly payment. The plains became British tea country, part of Bengal and Assam, and Bhutan lost its best farmland and trade routes. The war helped bring to power the Wangchuck family of central Bhutan, whose head became the first king of the Wangchuck dynasty. In the Treaty of Punakha of 1910 the yearly payment was doubled.
sum: The Duar War was fought between Bhutan and British India in 1864 and 1865 over the Duars, the fertile plains along the foot of the hills.
